paper_name: Release Enforcement in Resource-Oriented Partitioned Scheduling for Multiprocessor Systems
paper_description: Introduces release enforcement in ROP to shape higher-priority interference as sporadic, analyzes schedulability for segmented self-suspending tasks with one non-nested critical section, achieving 6x speedup factor.

formal_description.statement: ROP: Assign each shared resource R to a sync processor P_R; critical sections on P_R, non-critical on app processors; tasks partitioned statically.
formal_description.conclusion: Focuses partitioning on resources not tasks

informal_sketch.intuition: Resources as bottleneck; dedicate processors to sync.
steps: Execute CS on P_R, NCS elsewhere

formal_description.statement: RE: Delay job release until previous completes on its processor, shaping interference to sporadic pattern.

steps: On migration, wait for prior job finish

formal_description.statement: Under ROP+RE, response time R_i <= C_i + I_hp(R_i) + B_i, where I_hp sporadic interference, B_i blocking <= sum CS lengths.
formal_description.conclusion: Schedulable if R_i <= D_i via fixed-point

steps: Fixed-point R_i = C_i + sum I_hp_j(R_i) + B_i
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def rta_rop_re(task_i, hp_tasks, m):
    R = task_i.C
    while True:
        I = sum(dbf_j(task_j, R) for task_j in hp_tasks) / m
        B = sum(cs_lengths for cs in task_i.cs)
        new_R = task_i.C + I + B
        if new_R >= R: break
        R = new_R
    return R <= task_i.D
